This study presents a communication-aware multi-agent reinforcement learning framework, implemented as a CommNet–GAT fused variant of Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG), for collective coordination of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) swarms in a simulated bushfire-monitoring task. The framework augments decentralised agent policies with range-constrained structured messages, CommNet-based neighbour aggregation, and an adaptive gating mechanism for fusing local and shared information. The approach is evaluated in a simulated partially observable disaster monitoring environment, using bushfire monitoring as a representative case study. The results show that explicit communication substantially improves cooperative fire detection, collision avoidance, and formation behaviour under the considered simulation conditions. The proposed fusion configuration achieved a fire-detection rate of 99.5\\\\% and reduced inter-agent and obstacle collisions relative to the no-communication configuration. Evaluation across a limited range of team sizes also indicated that the learned communication structure can be applied without changing the underlying actor architecture.
